validity.recommendation: No action — existence, commodity, classification, and duplicate checks all pass.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, heavily documented, 15+ years of coverage in independent outlets across two countries (Reuters, The Diplomat, NPR, Dawn, VOA, Al Jazeera, Pakistan Today, ISSI, ICWA, dozens more). Iran's ~1,150km domestic section was physically completed years ago (NIOC/Ministry of Petroleum investment); the Pakistani ~780km section was formally inaugurated in 2013 (Zardari/Ahmadinejad ceremony) and has an approved-but-unbuilt 80km Gwadar-border segment (Pakistan CCoE, Feb/Mar 2024). This is not a GEM-only/hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are both correct — every independent source describes a large-diameter (56in) international transmission trunk carrying South Pars gas into Pakistan's national grid, not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 6-row Pakistan-gas roster — P0766 (TAPI, a different quadrilateral project via Afghanistan), P3101 (Pakistan Stream, Karachi-based, a separate Russia-linked proposal), P3173 (Somiani-Nawabshah, a purely domestic Balochistan-Sindh line unrelated to Iran), P3174 (Off-Shore, undefined endpoints) and P3178 (Sawan-Lahore, a domestic Sindh-Punjab trunk). None of these describe the Iran-to-Pakistan international corridor; P0452 is not a relabel/segment-double-count of any of them.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet records StartYear1=2024 with no ref (MISSING_REF). I could not verify that construction actually began in 2024. What independently verifies: Pakistan's caretaker cabinet (CCoE) approved, on Feb 24 2024 and again Mar 29 2024, a plan to build an 80km border-to-Gwadar segment ($158m) specifically to avoid an Iranian breach claim (Dawn, world-energy.org, both dated Feb 2024). But by the time of Iran's Nov 2024 arbitration filing at the Paris ICC ($18bn claim) and subsequent reporting through Jan 2026, no source reports land acquisition, groundbreaking, or any pipe laid on the Pakistani side — one search summary explicitly states 'the land in Gwadar earmarked for construction has yet to be acquired.' 2024 therefore looks like the year of a paper/cabinet approval, not an actual construction start, and by 2026 Pakistan is formally trying to abandon/settle the project rather than build it (see status_reviews). Recommend treating StartYear1=2024 as unverified/likely incorrect for an actual physical start.

validity.recommendation: Consider adding a Pakistan-side co-owner (e.g. Inter State Gas Systems / Petroleum Division, GoP) rather than 100% Iran Ministry of Petroleum, since the Pakistani segment is a separate national asset/liability under ISGS, not Iranian-owned. Left unstaged — a specific ownership % split would be a guess, not a verified fact; flagging for human judgment rather than forcing a fill (per entity_lookup / no-duplicate-entity and no-fabrication rules).
validity.researcher_notes: Owner1 = 'Iran Ministry of Petroleum' at 100% is recorded with no ref (MISSING_REF). Independent sources consistently describe a two-sided ownership structure: Iran's National Iranian Oil Company (under the Ministry of Petroleum) built and owns the ~1,150km Iranian section; Pakistan's Inter State Gas Systems (ISGS, a wholly state-owned company under the Petroleum Division) is the counterparty responsible for financing/building/owning the Pakistani ~780km section (Wikipedia: 'In Pakistan, InterState Gas Systems manages construction'; world-energy.org, Feb 2024, names ISGS as the entity NIOC served its Dec 2023 breach notice on). A single 100%-Iran owner record describes only the built (Iranian) portion and omits Pakistan's own stake/liability in its unbuilt segment. This is a caveat, not a hard error, since GEM may be scoping ownership to the entity that actually built physical asset to date.

validity.recommendation: Length, diameter and capacity values pass corroboration but carry cross-source caveats worth a note in ResearcherNotes: (1) length has a genuine, unresolved cross-source conflict; (2) diameter reflects only the built Iranian section.
validity.researcher_notes: CAPACITY (750 MMcf/d): independently confirmed — world-energy.org (Feb 19 2024, genuinely separate origin) quotes the original 2009 supply agreement as '750 MMCFD for 25 years from South Pars,' matching the existing offshore-technology.com ref exactly; note offshore-technology.com and oilandgasadvancement.com share identical boilerplate wording (same GlobalData/Verdict-Media project-database network) so they count as ONE source for corroboration purposes, not two — world-energy.org is the genuinely independent second leg. DIAMETER (56in): confirmed as the Iranian section's diameter (offshore-technology.com, matches existing ref) and is the figure universally quoted as 'the' pipeline diameter, but multiple sources (Wikipedia; offshore-technology.com itself) note the still-unbuilt Pakistani section is designed for a narrower 42in pipe — 56in is accurate for what's actually built, worth a note that it's Iran-side spec. LENGTH (2,775km): matches the commonly repeated headline total (Wikipedia's stated total; The Diplomat, the existing ref). However there is a real, unresolved conflict across sources: the offshore-technology.com/oilandgasadvancement.com network states an internally-consistent total of 1,880km (1,100km Iran + 780km Pakistan), and even Wikipedia's own segment breakdown (1,172km Iran + 785km Pakistan = 1,957km) doesn't sum to its own stated 2,775km total. 2,775km is still the most-repeated figure across sources including the sheet's own existing ref, so I'm not proposing a change, but flagging that GEM's number does not have a clean, fully-reconciled cross-source derivation.

fills.researcher_notes: Two independent outlets (world-energy.org, Feb 2024; domain-b.com) both name South Pars as the gas source, matching the sheet's recorded value exactly.

NPR (2013, genuinely independent outlet) states the line runs 'from Assaluyeh along Iran's Persian Gulf coast...to Nawabshah in Pakistan's Sindh province' — confirming both endpoints in one sentence, matching the sheet exactly. offshore-technology.com corroborates Nawabshah as the Pakistani off-take point and Bushehr province as the Iranian origin region. CAVEAT: Wikipedia's Iran-Pakistan gas pipeline article instead names Multan, Punjab as the ultimate terminus and never mentions Nawabshah — a genuine cross-source conflict. I'm filling the ref because two independent, verified sources directly support the sheet's existing Nawabshah/Sindh value, but flagging the Wikipedia discrepancy for awareness. (A third source, ICWA's analysis, also supports Nawabshah but its URL fails url_verifier with an SSLError, so it is not cited.)

offshore-technology.com states '$7.5bn pipeline' matching the sheet exactly. domain-b.com (genuinely independent origin) corroborates a project cost in the same range but is internally inconsistent between its headline ('$7.5 billion') and body text ('$7.6 billion') — a ~1.3% variance I read as rounding/reporting noise rather than a material conflict, so I'm filling the ref rather than raising a spec concern, at tier=medium given the minor discrepancy in the second source.

Could not verify StartYear1=2024 as an actual construction start — see the paired validity concern (concern_type=spec) above. The only 2024 event I can independently confirm is a Feb/Mar 2024 Pakistani cabinet APPROVAL to build an 80km segment, not ground-breaking; multiple sources through late 2024/2026 indicate no physical construction ever began and Pakistan is now (Jan 2026) trying to abandon the project. Leaving MISSING_REF rather than fabricating support for a value I believe is likely wrong.

Not filling a ref for 100% Iran Ministry of Petroleum ownership — see the paired validity concern (concern_type=attribution) above. Sources describe a two-sided structure (NIOC/Ministry of Petroleum for Iran's built section; Pakistan's ISGS for the unbuilt Pakistani section), so a bare 100%-Iran record likely needs a second owner row rather than a supporting citation for the current single-owner value. Deferring to human judgment / entity_lookup rather than guessing a % split.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The recorded Status='construction' (LastUpdated 2025-07-11) is stale and, on the evidence, was probably never really accurate for the Pakistani side. Timeline: Feb/Mar 2024 — Pakistan's CCoE approved building an 80km border-to-Gwadar segment ($158m) purely to avoid an Iranian breach claim, but land in Gwadar was never acquired and no construction followed (Dawn, world-energy.org, both Feb 2024). Nov 2024 — Iran filed an $18bn arbitration claim at the Paris ICC over Pakistan's non-construction (multiple outlets). Jan 2026 — three independent Pakistani/trade outlets, all url_verifier-confirmed, report Pakistan formally notifying Iran it intends to place the project on hold and pursue an out-of-court settlement to abandon it (digitalpakistan.pk, Jan 14 2026: 'Pakistan has formally conveyed to Iran that it intends to place the Iran-Pakistan (IP) gas pipeline project on hold'; pipeline-journal.net, Jan 15 2026: 'Pakistan has notified Iran of its intention to abandon the long-stalled Iran-Pakistan (IP) gas pipeline project through an out-of-court settlement'), while a parallel legal track (thenews.pk, Jan 23 2026) has Pakistan simultaneously requesting a 10-year extension to 2035 to avoid the $18bn arbitration penalty, with a verdict expected 2027-28 if no settlement is reached — i.e. Pakistan is hedging between abandonment and a decade-long extension, but under NEITHER track is actual construction proceeding. Both the 'abandon via settlement' and the '10-year extension' framings describe a project that is on the shelf, not under construction, so I'm proposing Status=shelved (ShelvedCancelledType=Confirmed, since this is an explicitly reported decision, not the mechanical dormancy rule) rather than 'cancelled' (Pakistan has explicitly left revival on the table, contingent on a US sanctions waiver) or 'proposed' (there IS an existing signed agreement and a built Iranian half, so 'proposed' understates it). NEWER, non-decisive signal: by April-June 2026, several outlets (Pakistan Today Apr 11 2026, ProPakistani, Express Tribune, Global Connectivities Jun 2026) report 'revival hopes rise' after US-Iran peace talks/an Islamabad-mediated ceasefire process, with an unnamed expert saying a sanctions rollback 'could create room to restart work' — but this is speculative/conditional language, not a report of construction actually resuming, so it does not change my verdict; it does mean this determination should be re-checked again soon given how fluid the situation is.

summary: P0452 (Iran-Pakistan Pipeline) is a real, well-documented project — not a duplicate or misclassification — but Status='construction' is stale/likely wrong (change to 'shelved', high tier, 3 independent Jan-2026 sources) and StartYear1=2024 plus 100%-Iran ownership are unverified/questionable (flagged as spec and attribution concerns, left UNRESOLVED rather than force-filled); FuelSource, Location (Nawabshah/Sindh, despite a Wikipedia vs. NPR/offshore-technology conflict with Multan), and SegmentCost were successfully filled with verified independent refs.
